about_this_copy.what: NASA CR-2144 (Heffley and Jewell, 'Aircraft Handling Qualities Data', December 1972), Section IV, the F-4C, as data: its tables of flight conditions, dimensional derivatives, transfer-function factors and handling-qualities parameters, its control-system diagrams, and its plotted curves measured from the page images.
about_this_copy.made_from: The full transcription made for FSG milestone 3 on 26 November 2026 (390 KB). It and its reading notes were working files of the session that made them, and are not in the repo.
left_out_of_this_copy: The four thrust-input transfer-function tables (IV-5, IV-7, IV-9, IV-11). The game has no use for them: thrust is the engine model's. The numerators of IV-7, IV-9 and IV-11 were read only once.

Each table row's cells 'as printed' (the same numbers as text). They are kept, as 'printed', only in a row where a printed cell is not the value used: a blank, a dash, a parenthesis, or a misprint (each misprint is in its table's 'doubt' list with the reason).
about_this_copy.paths: Paths that start work/ or refs/ are in the transcription's working folder, not in this repo. The report is NASA CR-2144, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19730003312; its F-4C section is PDF pages 67 to 113 (printed 61 to 107).

F/C 1 is the power-approach configuration (33197 lb, c.g. .291 MGC); F/C 2-10 are the nominal clean configuration (38925 lb in the tables, '38924 lb' on the figures; c.g. .289 MGC = 28.9% of the mean geometric chord). background.source: OCR text of the page, corrected by eye
text: The F-4C is an Air Force tactical fighter whose primary mission is all-weather air-to-air missile combat. Lateral control is achieved by ailerons in combination with spoilers on a swept wing. A swept stabilator provides longitudinal stability and control. Directional stability and control is accomplished through a conventional fin-rudder combination. Landing speed is reduced by full span leading edge flaps and inboard plain trailing edge flaps in conjunction with blowing-type boundary layer control (BLC). Boundary layer control is automatically induced when full flap deflection occurs.

Features distinguishing the USAF F-4C from its Navy counterpart, the F-4B, are: Lack of drooped ailerons with flaps down resulting in higher landing speeds. Dual flight controls resulting in slightly increased control system inertia. Wing bumps to house larger main gear wheels resulting in a slight drag increase.

Data included here was obtained primarily from MAC Report No. 9842. Special emphasis is placed on the longitudinal control system because of its relative complexity when compared to other aircraft. Figure IV-4 has been added to help illustrate this system. Also, care has been taken to retain some of the control system nomenclature used by the manufacturer, e.g., qB and PBF (see Fig. IV-5).

The Stability Augmentation block diagrams are shown in Fig. IV-7. The roll SAS described is not included in lateral directional SAS on transfer functions since it is faded out with the lateral control stick out of neutral position.

quote: The following shorthand notation is used to print the factored polynomials for all transfer functions*:  (s + 1/Tx)_i = 1/Tx_i , i = 1 to k ;  (s^2 + 2 zeta omega_n s + omega_n^2)_j = zeta_j; omega_n_j , j = 1 to l ;  where k + 2l = n, the order of the polynomial

COMPUTER PRINT OUT / STANDARD NOTATION, DEFINITION:  DET - Roots of the denominator;  N(X/Y) - Numerator N^x_y;  A(X) - Gain of the transfer function x/y;  1/T(X)I - 1/Tx_i, rad/sec;  Z(X)J - zeta_j;  W(X)J - omega_n_j, rad/sec
*The transfer function x/y is written as: x/y = N^x_y / Delta = A_x (s^m + s^(m-1) + ... s^0) / (s^n + s^(n-1) + ... s^0)
Any roots enclosed in parentheses imply the opposite order of what is specified, e.g., Z(DET)1 = (0.00132) => 1/T(DET)1 = 0.00132
in_practice: A parenthesised pair printed on a Z(...)/W(...) row pair is two real roots 1/T (e.g. Table IV-4 F/C 2: Z(DET)1 = (-.0378), W(DET)1 = ( .0516) means (s - .0378)(s + .0516): an unstable 'tuck' root and a stable one in place of a phugoid pair).
A parenthesised pair printed on two consecutive 1/T(...) rows is a complex pair: first zeta, then omega (e.g. Table IV-4 F/C 1: 1/T(U)2 = ( .452), 1/T(U)3 = ( .561) means zeta = .452, omega = .561).
A single parenthesised value on a Z row with a blank W row (Table IV-6 F/C 2, Z(DET)1 = ( 25.3)) is one real root.
A root is (s + 1/T): positive 1/T is stable. The gain A is the ratio of leading coefficients (denominator made monic).
The example's last factor is printed in the report as '1.13^2 s^2' [sic].

quote: Transfer functions are always given for body axis motion quantities. Handling qualities parameters are also given in the body axis. All acceleration transfer functions (a_z' and a_y') are for the pilot's position. Thrust transfer functions do not include any engine response characteristics.

The coefficients are based on rigid wind tunnel data, estimated flexible data, or flight test results, depending upon availability. This is indicated by the words "rigid," "flexible," and "flight" on each aero data plot. Also, the axis system is indicated by "stability" for a body-fixed stability axis system or "body" for a body-fixed system aligned with the F.R.L.

Although only SAS-off values are shown, the definitions given in Appendix A are general and could be used in conjunction with the SAS-on transfer functions to yield SAS-on handling qualities parameters.

XB, YB, ZB - The Body-Axis System consists of right-handed, orthogonal axes whose origin is fixed at the nominal aircraft center of gravity. Its orientation remains fixed with respect to the aircraft, the XB and ZB axes being in the plane of symmetry. The exact alignment of XB axis is arbitrary, herein it is taken along the body centerline reference.

XS, YS, ZS - The Stability-Axis System is that particular body-axis system for which the XS axis is coincident with the projection of the total steady-state velocity vector (VTo) on the aircraft's plane of symmetry. Its orientation remains fixed with respect to the aircraft.

mnemonics.source: OCR text checked against the tables

table_IV_2.C.G.(MGC): center of gravity relative to mean geometric chord
table_IV_2.IX, IY, IZ, IXZ: body axis (FRL) moments of inertia, slug-ft^2
table_IV_2.EPSILON(DEG): inclination of principal axis with respect to FRL, degrees
table_IV_2.LXP(FT): x distance to pilot, ft (positive forward)
table_IV_2.LZP(FT): z distance to pilot, ft (positive down)
table_IV_2.ITH(DEG): thrust incidence with respect to FRL, degrees
table_IV_2.XI(DEG): xi_0 = i_th + alpha_0, degrees [as defined in Appendix A; the F-4C table prints 5.25 for every flight condition, i.e. equal to ITH]
table_IV_2.LTH(FT): perpendicular distance to thrust line from c.g., ft (positive for nose-up pitching moment due to thrust)

longitudinal.XDTH, ZDTH: ft/sec^2 per lb of thrust (1/m and its component)
longitudinal.MDTH: rad/sec^2 per lb of thrust (= LTH/IY)
longitudinal.AZP: a_z' at the pilot station, ft/sec^2 (positive down)

lateral.AYP: a_y' at lx, lz (pilot station), ft/sec^2

longitudinal.D(G)/D(U) (DEG/KT): d gamma / d u, degrees/knot, at s = 0
longitudinal.NZA (G/RAD): N_z_alpha, g/rad = -(U0/g) N^az_delta(s)/N^w_delta(s) at s = 0 (constant speed)
longitudinal.DE/G (DEG/G): delta_e/g, degrees/g (here stabilator per g), constant speed, s = 0
longitudinal.PHUGOID(2) (TUCK(2)): the phugoid time to double amplitude, seconds = ln 2/|zeta_ph omega_ph| for zeta_ph < 0; printed in parentheses when it is the time to double of a real 'tuck' root
longitudinal.1/C(1/10): short period inverse cycles to 1/10 amplitude = (2 pi/ln 10) sqrt(zeta_sp^2/(1 - zeta_sp^2)) for 0 <= zeta_sp < 1
longitudinal.FST/KT (LB/KT): stick force per knot, pounds/knot, s = 0
longitudinal.FST/G (LB/G): stick force per g, pounds per g, constant speed, s = 0
longitudinal.--: The parameter has no meaning or is not defined at this flight condition

lateral.DR PERIOD (SEC): Dutch roll period = 2 pi/(omega_d sqrt(1 - zeta_d^2))
lateral.1/C(1/2): Dutch roll inverse cycles to 1/2 amplitude = (2 pi/ln 2) sqrt(zeta_d^2/(1 - zeta_d^2)), for zeta_d >= 0
lateral.SPIRAL (2) (SEC): spiral time to double amplitude = Ts ln 2, for 1/Ts <= 0
lateral.P(I): roll rate at peak I for a unit step input of delta_a
lateral.W(PHI)/W(D): ratio of the roll (phi numerator) frequency to the Dutch roll frequency
lateral.DEL-B-MAX: maximum sideslip excursion at the c.g., occurring within two seconds or one half-period of the Dutch roll, whichever is greater, for a step aileron-control command
lateral.PHI TO BETA, PHASE: phase of phi/beta at the Dutch-roll root, degrees
lateral.PHI TO VE: |phi/v_e| at the Dutch-roll root, deg/fps; v_e = beta x V_EAS, V_EAS = sqrt(2 q/rho_0)

equations_of_motion.verified: read from the page images and confirmed numerically: they reproduce Tables IV-4, IV-5, IV-14, IV-15 from Tables IV-2, IV-3, IV-13
longitudinal: [(1 - X_u-dot)s - X_u*] u + [-X_w-dot s - X_w] w + [(-X_q + W0)s + g cos(theta0)] theta = X_delta delta
[-Z_u-dot s - Z_u*] u + [(1 - Z_w-dot)s - Z_w] w + [(-Z_q - U0)s + g sin(theta0)] theta = Z_delta delta
[-M_u-dot s - M_u*] u - [M_w-dot s + M_w] w + [s^2 - M_q s] theta = M_delta delta
q = s theta;  h-dot = -w cos(theta0) + u sin(theta0) + (U0 cos(theta0) + W0 sin(theta0)) theta;  a_z = s w - U0 q + (g sin theta0) theta;  a_z' = a_z - l_x s^2 theta
NOTE: Terms including X_u-dot, Z_u-dot, M_u-dot, X_w-dot are neglected in polynomial expressions.
U0 = VTo cos(alpha0), W0 = VTo sin(alpha0), theta0 = alpha0 + gamma0
lateral: (s - Y_v) beta - [(W0 s + g cos theta0)/VTo] (p/s) + [(U0 s - g sin theta0)/(VTo s)] r = Y*_delta delta
-L'_beta beta + s(s - L'_p)(p/s) - L'_r r = L'_delta delta
-N'_beta beta - N'_p s (p/s) + (s - N'_r) r = N'_delta delta
v = VTo beta;  phi = p/s + (r/s) tan theta0;  a_y = s v + U0 r - W0 p - g (cos theta0) phi;  a_y' = a_y + l_x s r - l_z s p

figures.legend: Each curve is a list of [Mach, value, flag]. flag m = measured (pixel centre of the drawn line against the axis ticks), i = interpolated between measured neighbours (dash gap, or under a circled flight-condition marker), e = eyeballed (read off a gridded enlargement; line could not be isolated), k = measured under a marker. Curve keys are altitudes in feet ('SL' = sea level). Points every 0.1 Mach, every 0.05 from 0.8 to 1.2, plus the ends of each drawn curve (ends are good to about 0.02 Mach).

method: Reference quantities: S = 530 ft^2, c-bar = 16.04 ft, b = 38.67 ft, m = W/g with g = 32.174 ft/sec^2, q = Q(PSF) and V = VTO(FPS) of Table IV-2, IY, IX, IZ, IXZ of Table IV-2.

Body-axis derivatives of Table IV-3 are first rotated to stability axes through alpha0 (inverse of the report's Appendix B transformation): Zw_s = Zw cos^2(a) - (Zu + Xw) sin(a) cos(a) + Xu sin^2(a);  Mw_s = Mw cos(a) - Mu sin(a);  Zd_s = Zd cos(a) - Xd sin(a).

CL_alpha = -Zw_s m V/(q S) - CD (CD from the digitised CD curve);  Cm_alpha = Mw_s IY V/(q S c);  Cm_q = 2 V IY Mq/(q S c^2);  Cm_alpha_dot = 2 V^2 IY Mwd/(q S c^2);  CL_delta_s = -Zd_s m/(q S);  Cm_delta_s = Md IY/(q S c).

Lateral (extra): Cy_beta = Yv m V/(q S). L = L' - (IXZ/IX) N', N = N' - (IXZ/IZ) L' (unpriming); body-axis Cl = L IX/(q S b), Cn = N IZ/(q S b); rotated to stability axes: Cl_s = Cl cos(a) + Cn sin(a), Cn_s = Cn cos(a) - Cl sin(a).
Plotted values are the digitised curves interpolated at the flight-condition Mach number (the curve there lies under the circled marker, so it is an interpolation between neighbours).
other_identities: Table IV-2: VTO(KTAS) = M x a(h) (1962 standard atmosphere) reproduces all ten values to the knot; Q = 0.7 p M^2 reproduces Q within 0.4% (the 45,000 and 55,000 ft columns imply a static pressure 0.3% above the 1962 standard; F/C 1 prints 62.6 against 62.9); QC follows the subsonic isentropic / supersonic Rayleigh pitot formulas within 0.3%.
Table IV-13: YB = VTO x YV in all ten columns (within rounding).

Tables IV-4 and IV-5 recomputed from IV-2/IV-3 with the Appendix C equations: all short-period, phugoid/tuck and numerator factors within 1.5% except (a) small phugoid-related roots sensitive to third-digit rounding (F/C 1 phugoid damping .096 computed, .102 printed; F/C 4 tuck roots -.0625/.0753 computed, -.0612/.0741 printed) and (b) the F/C 1 thrust numerators, whose printed gain implies MDTH about 3% smaller than printed.
Tables IV-14 and IV-15 recomputed from IV-2/IV-13 (with L'DA of F/C 6 = 10.0): Dutch roll, roll and numerator factors within 1.5%; spiral roots within 8% (they are small differences of large terms).
Table IV-12: NZA = (U0/g)(-Zw + Zd Mw/Md) reproduces all ten values within 1% (this is what fixes ZW = -.494 at F/C 9); CAP = W(DET)2^2/NZA within 1%; tuck times = ln2/|1/T|; 1/C(1/10) from Z(DET)2.
Table IV-18: DR PERIOD and 1/C(1/2) follow from Z(DET)1, W(DET)1 of Table IV-14 in all ten columns; W(PHI)/W(D) = W(PHI)1/W(DET)1; SPIRAL(2) = ln2/.000179.
Stick-force numerator gains (IV-6): A(THE)_FST/A(THE)_DS = -31.8 in F/C 1-7 = (-3.36/57.3) x 20 / .0369 (gearing x actuator pole / feel inertia).
Trim CL lines of the CL-CD figure equal W/(q S) (measured/computed 1.007-1.026).
comments: Agreement is 0-2% for the five requested longitudinal derivatives at both flight conditions, except Cm_alpha at F/C 2 (-0.269 from the tables against -0.29 interpolated): the sea-level Cm_alpha curve has a knee exactly under marker 2, whose centre reads about -0.27, so the table value is the better number there.
Cn_delta_a at F/C 6 differs by 0.0005, which is the reading error of that plot (the curve crosses zero under marker 6).
The lateral-directional comparison confirms that Table IV-13 is in body axes and primed, and that the plots are in stability axes.
